claim_or_issue: Job boards contribute 26.9% of hires and should be prioritised
metric: Job Board share of hires (Source as recorded, primary; DEC-017)
actual_value: 26.9% (7/26) Source as recorded; definition sensitivity 23.1% (M-A2) to 30.8% (M-A8); one hire = 3.8 pp
calculation_method: Stage=Hired joined to Candidates.Source; variants M-A1, M-A2, M-A3, M-A8, M-A9, M-A10 (metric_calculations.csv)
evidence: M-A0, M-A1, M-A2, M-A3, M-A8, M-A9, M-A10, M-A5, M-A7*-Job Board, M-A9n; DQ-01, DQ-02, DQ-04
product_implication: The share reproduces, but prioritisation does not follow from it: Job Board is 67.4% of applications and converts at 2.7% to 3.4% per application across all attribution variants, the lowest of any channel with hires (next lowest 9.7%). Referral is NOT a proven high-performing channel: 7/7 Referral-labelled hires have no referrer link. No data measures integration friction.

claim_or_issue: Offer acceptance is approximately 72% and needs improvement
metric: Decided-offer acceptance rate, offer-level (provisional primary; DEC-016)
actual_value: 83.9% (26/31) decided offers, offer-level; all-issued-offer ratio 72.2% (26/36); candidate-level 85.7% (24/28); scenarios 76.5% (stale Pending as expired, provisional cutoff), 72.2% (same, extraction-date cutoff), 86.1% (upper bound); one decided offer = 3.2 pp
calculation_method: Offers.Status; variants M-B0..M-B5, M-B9, M-B10
confidence: Medium (4 of 5 Pending carry decision dates)
product_implication: The VP's ~72% is the all-issued-offer ratio (26/36), which counts 5 unresolved Pending offers as non-acceptance. The provisional decided-offer rate is 83.9%. Whether that needs improvement cannot be judged (no target or benchmark). The data does show unreliable offer-status records (DQ-06, DQ-07).
